newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian banks lead blue chips higher.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian banks lead blue chips higher.

text.p: Lithuanian blue chips closed higher as the country's leading banks extended their recent gains in heavier trade on Thursday, dealers said.
But the rest of the market eased as the country's cautious investors continued to favour proven blue chips over the rest of the pack.
The official list, which tracks the five leading stocks, jumped 21.65 points to 1000.24 points while the wider group-A list sagged 18.38 points to 1834.78 points by the close.
Central market turnover bounded up to 1.1 million litas from 527,000 litas.

Official list stock Hermis Bank soared to 241 litas from 229 litas, near its all-time high of 245 litas, in central market turnover of 200,000 litas. Brokers say it may pass its old mark but take a short break afterwards.
"I think 250 litas will be the limit for the next week," one broker said.
Rival Vilniaus bank traded at 253 litas from 249 litas, closing in on its all-time high of 260 litas, in central market turnover of 214,000 litas.
Brokers have been bullish on Vilniaus Bank since it reported audited profits for the first six months that were almost double what they were in the same period last year.
"I think they'll do better in the third and fourth quarters," said one broker.
Rokishkis Cheese, which also reported impressive first half profits, advanced only slightly, to 44.50 litas from 44 litas in central market turnover of 49,000 litas.
